info.name: kafka-06-producer-consumer-masterclass
info.description:
Full test suite for kafka-06-producer-consumer-masterclass.

Before running:
1. docker compose up -d
2. mvn spring-boot:run

App runs on http://localhost:8080

item.name: Producer Patterns
item.description: All producer send patterns from sync to transactional

request.description:
Synchronous send.
The HTTP response is only returned AFTER Kafka acknowledges the write.

Expect:
- HTTP 200 with a MessageEvent JSON body
- Logs: [SYNC] topic=general-topic partition=X offset=Y
- Listener logs: [GROUP-A], [GROUP-B], [METADATA], [REPLAY] all fire

Async fire-and-forget with a callback.
HTTP 200 is returned immediately — Kafka delivery is handled in the background.

Expect:
- HTTP 200 instantly
- Logs (slightly after): [ASYNC-CALLBACK] OK — partition=X offset=Y
- Same listener logs as sync

Async send returning a CompletableFuture.
Spring MVC suspends the HTTP response until the future completes — no thread blocked.

Expect:
- HTTP 200 with text: 'Delivered — partition=X offset=Y'
- Logs: [FUTURE] Delivered to partition=X offset=Y

Keyed send with key='priority1'.
Routed to a deterministic partition. Consumed by the priority filter listener only.

Expect:
- HTTP 200 with MessageEvent
- Logs: [PRIORITY-1] HIGH-PRIORITY message received: ...
- [OTHER-PRIORITY] listener does NOT fire
- [ERROR-HANDLER] fires (same topic, different factory) and retries 2x

Keyed send with a non-priority key.
Only the 'other priority' consumer fires (priority-1 consumer filters this out).

Expect:
- HTTP 200 with MessageEvent
- Logs: [OTHER-PRIORITY] Standard message received: ...
- [PRIORITY-1] listener does NOT fire

Transactional send — all 3 messages committed atomically.

Expect:
- HTTP 200 with a JSON array of 3 MessageEvent objects
- Logs: [TRANSACTIONAL] Queued message (x3), then Committed 3 message(s)
- Consumer logs: [TRANSACTIONAL] Committed message received: ... (x3)

Transactional send — 'fail' key triggers a rollback.
NOTHING is visible to consumers — not even the first 'success' message.

Expect:
- HTTP 500 (RuntimeException propagates)
- Logs: [TRANSACTIONAL] Encountered key='fail' — rolling back...
- Consumer logs: ZERO [TRANSACTIONAL] entries

item.name: Consumer — Manual API
item.description: Low-level consumer: seek to specific partition + offset

request.description:
Read all messages in partition 0 starting from offset 0.
Send a few messages via the producer endpoints first, then call this.

Expect:
- HTTP 200 with a JSON array of MessageEvent objects
- Logs: [MANUAL-CONSUMER] Reading ... Fetched N record(s)

Read from partition 1. The general topic has 2 partitions (0 and 1).
Messages are distributed across both depending on keys used.
